trace them to check the count. | | mis:loop_control->DoubleLoopIndexCount | wrong rule: for (double x = 0.0; x <= 1.0; x += 0.1) runs exactly 11 times. | right rule: Using a double as a for-loop index is legal but bad practice: the number of iterations depends on an equality test between double values, which may not give the result you expect. | | mis:loop_control->ForLoopPartSkipped | wrong rule: A pass of a loop may leave out one of its parts (the condition test, the body, the update, or the initialization). | right rule: Each pass of a for loop runs test, then body, then update, every time; the initialization runs once, at the start. | | mis:loop_control->ForUpdateBeforeBody | wrong rule: The update part of a for header (e.g. i = i - 4) runs before the body on each pass, so the first pass already sees the updated value. | right rule: The update runs after the body, before the next condition test; the first pass uses the initial value. | | mis:loop_control->IdiomOverridesCode | wrong rule: An array loop processes the whole array from index 0 to length-1 and increments its index at the end of the body, whatever the code says. | right rule: The loop visits exactly the indices that its initialisation, guard and update produce, in the order in which its statements are written. | | mis:loop_control->InfiniteLoopUnnoticed | wrong rule: A while loop always stops on its own, even if nothing in its body can make the condition false. | right rule: A while loop stops only when its condition is false at a check, so if no pass changes the variables in the condition, it never stops. | | mis:loop_control->LoopHeaderIsEquations | wrong rule: The initialization, condition and update of a for header are equations that all hold at the same time. | right rule: The three header parts are statements run at different moments: init once, then condition test, body, update, repeated. | | mis:loop_control->LoopStepAlwaysOne | wrong rule: A loop variable always goes up or down by 1, whatever the update says (so i = i - 4 is read as i--). | right rule: The loop variable changes exactly as the update expression says (i += 2, i = i - 4, i *= 2, ...). | | mis:loop_control->LoopUpdateChangesDirection | wrong rule: The update of the loop variable can change from pass to pass (e.g. switch direction) although the code is the same. | right rule: The update expression is the same on every pass; the loop variable changes by the rule written in the update. | | mis:loop_control->OffByOneBound | wrong rule: i < n and i <= n mean the same, so the loop runs until i equals n and the last pass can use a[n]. | right rule: for (i = 0; i < n; i++) runs n times with i going up to n - 1; with <= it runs n + 1 times and reaches i = n. | | mis:loop_control->PreIncrementBeforeLoop | wrong rule: With ++i in the update of for (int i = s; i < n; ++i), i is increased before the body runs, so the first pass uses s + 1. | right rule: The update runs after each pass of the body, so with either ++i or i++ the first pass uses i = s. |
